Iam supra (p. 194) monuimus caput quod in libro Angelico haec sequitur, fortasse
eiusdem scriptoris esse. Cuius capitis versus nonnullos ex codice Mediolanensi
descriptos petentibus nobis misit Dominicus Bassi, qua semper est liberalitate.
sections.en: We have already warned above (p. 194) that the chapter which follows these things in the Angelicus book is perhaps of the same writer. Some lines of this chapter copied from the Milanese codex Dominicus Bassi sent to us requesting them, with the liberality which he always has.

sections.text:
1 Anubin cynocephalum Cani caelesti adsimulatum esse ex ipsa eius natura
sequitur; cf. Boll, Sphaera, p. 179. Sed cum Anubis mortuorum sepulchrorumque
custos sit, peregrino deo Graeci Hecatam suam substituerunt. — Martem Caniculae
coniunctum esse alibi non invenimus; sine dubio quia sidus eius calidum esse
docebant astrologi, illam necessitudinem statuerunt.
2 Cf. Ps.-Eratosth., Cataster., 24 : Λύρα κατεσκευάσθη τὸ μὲν πρῶτον ὑπὸ
Ἑρμοῦ ἐκ τῆς χελώνης ... μετέλαβε δὲ αὐτὴν Ἀπόλλων. Cf. Hygin, Astr., II, 7.
3 Capricornum, Haedos, Capram Pani, pastorum deo, convenire manifestum est,
et Hermes, pater eius, saepe et in fabulis et in monumentis cum eo coniungitur.
Praetera mythographi Aegyptii narrabant Pana, cum Typhonem fugeret, in
flumen se deiecisse et Capricornum factum esse. Evhemerus quoque dixit Capram
fuisse Panos uxorem (Hygin, fab. II, 13 et 28). Cf. praeterea Boll, Sphaera,
p. 480.
4 Cur Kronos per filios suos Plutonem Neptunumque apparitiones provocet et
auxilium praebeat, nobis quidem non omnino perspicuum est.
sections.en:
1 That the dog-headed Anubis was likened to the celestial Dog follows from his very nature; cf. Boll, Sphaera, p. 179. But since Anubis is the guardian of the dead and of tombs, the Greeks substituted their Hecate for the foreign god. — That Mars is joined to the Dog-star we have not found elsewhere; without doubt because the astrologers taught that his star is hot, they established that connection.
2 Cf. Ps.-Eratosth., Cataster., 24: The Lyre was constructed first by Hermes from the tortoise ... but Apollo took it over. Cf. Hygin, Astr., II, 7.
3 That Capricorn, the Kids, the Goat suit Pan, the god of shepherds, is manifest, and Hermes, his father, is often joined with him both in fables and in monuments. Besides, the Egyptian mythographers narrated that Pan, when he fled Typhon, threw himself into the river and was made Capricorn. Euhemerus also said that the Goat was the wife of Pan (Hygin, fab. II, 13 and 28). Cf. besides Boll, Sphaera, p. 480.
4 Why Kronos should provoke apparitions and offer help through his sons Pluto and Neptune is indeed not entirely clear to us.

summary.headline: Planetary Manifestations and Helps
summary.text: Astrological doctrine assigns visions, manifestations, helps, and therapies to Mars, Anubis, the Lyre, Capricorn, the Kids, the Goat, Pan, Hermes, Saturn, Pluto, Poseidon, and the benefic planets according to celestial places, aspects, diurnal or nocturnal birth, and planetary nature. Editorial notes discuss Anubis and the celestial Dog, the Lyre’s mythic origins, Pan’s association with Capricorn and the Goat, and Kronos’s sons.
